Porsche Golf Circle
UX / Product Design  ·  Experience Redesign  ·  2025
Overview
01
Challenge
How might we elevate the events digital experience within the Porsche Golf Circle to create stronger, more meaningful connections between users and the brand?
02
Role
UI/UX Designer — research, ideation, interaction design & high-fidelity prototype. Team of four across a 5-week sprint.
03
Methods
Stakeholder interviews · Desk research · 8 user interviews · Heuristic analysis (Nielsen) · Crazy 8s · Concept testing · High-fidelity prototyping in Figma.
PORSCHE
GOLF
CIRCLE
04
Problem
Golfers in the Porsche Golf Circle who value community and networking over competition struggle to connect with like-minded peers. The app's focus on competitive events limits ongoing interaction before, during, and after events.
05
Solution
Three feature pillars: Community & Connections (groups, QR invites, suggested contacts), Events & Experiences (redesigned IA, in-app booking, family events), and Live Scores (real-time leaderboard, interactive course map).
06
Impact
Higher user satisfaction · Increased event attendance · Elevated perceived value of the Porsche community as a destination beyond the car.
Process — 5 week sprint
Week 01 — Discover
Stakeholder Meeting & Desk Research
Onboarded with Porsche to understand the product and challenge. Synthesised certainties, suppositions, and doubts. Parallel desk research surfaced: active communities increase event attendance by 72% (McKinsey); over 40% of attendees report stronger brand loyalty post-event; 51% of club members have networks of 11+ golfers vs 27% for non-members.
Week 01–02 — Discover
User Research — 8 In-Depth Interviews
Remote interviews 45–60 min each. Three segments: Porsche owners (n=3), Golfers (n=3), Porsche owners who golf (n=2). Across Colombia, Brazil, Spain, Italy, Switzerland, Sweden. Themes: relationship with golf, brand loyalty, event journey, social connection, app retention.
Week 02–03 — Define
Heuristic Analysis & Synthesis
Evaluated the existing Porsche Golf Circle app against Nielsen's 10 heuristics. Three critical priorities identified: #3 User Control & Freedom (score 3 — no cancel flow in multi-step registration), #5 Error Prevention (score 3 — Handicap Index field lacks guidance), #8 Aesthetic & Minimalist Design (score 3 — hero images bury key event info). Three personas built: Alexander Sterling (elite golfer), Jay Simmons (family golfer), Robert Paulson (business-minded golfer).
Week 03 — Ideate
How Might We + Crazy 8s Brainstorming
Consolidated ideation into a single overarching HMW: elevate the experience to foster connections and networking among successful members through their shared passion for golf, while providing exclusive value to Porsche's official community. Crazy 8s generated concepts for live events, community groups, QR onboarding, stats integration, and family-facing event formats.
Week 04 — Prototype
Sketching, Wireframes & Concept Testing
Parallel sketching and Figma wireframing for three core flows. Concept tested with one participant (golfer, 58, Colombia). Key findings: score visibility needs higher contrast, hole-by-hole detail requested, in-app payment resonated strongly, event text size too small on mobile.
Week 04–05 — Deliver
High-Fidelity Prototype
Full hi-fi prototype in Figma across Community, Events, Score, and Home tabs. Maintained Porsche Golf Circle's dark palette and green accent system. Delivered interactive prototype link and FigJam process board to Porsche stakeholders.
Key Research Insights
▸ Connection
Golf is a medium for genuine connections — many members see tournaments as secondary to the social fabric of the sport. Community features were largely absent from the existing app.
Synthesis · User Research
▸ Family
Even highly-valued event invitations are declined to spend free time with friends and family. Friends and family are often the decision-makers for attendance.
Synthesis · User Research
▸ Aspirational Brand
"So these are like little breaks which make you feel important. Even if you're not owning the most special Porsche, you're the same to them." — Porsche owner, 27, Switzerland
Verbatim · User Interview
▸ Invisible Community
4 out of 5 Porsche owners interviewed — including golfers — had never heard of the Porsche Golf Circle. Community awareness is a critical gap upstream of any app improvement.
Synthesis · User Research
▸ Networking
"Being in a Porsche community would be beneficial for networking. Porsche owners are usually well-connected and it can open doors." — Porsche owner, 40, Spain
Verbatim · User Interview
▸ Social Golf
Among golfers who started in the last decade, the social aspect as a motivation rose from 23.8% to 37.4%. Social gatherings after tournaments are the primary connection moment.
